Update on Convertible Loan Note Instrument
Further to the Company's announcement of 6 July 2026, AIQ (LSE: AIQ) is pleased to announce that, on 14 August 2026, it issued further convertible loan notes of £250k to new noteholders under its convertible loan note instrument with China International Securities Ltd that was entered into on 3 July 2026 (the "New Loan Note Facility"). To date, the Company has issued convertible loan notes totalling £1.25m under the New Loan Facility.
The remaining loan notes of up to £750k to be issued under the New Loan Note Facility may be issued in tranches up to and including 31 August 2026. This follows the Board signing, on 14 August 2026, a deed of variation to extend the deadline for the issue of convertible loan notes under the New Loan Note Facility from 14 August 2026 to 31 August 2026 to allow sufficient time for satisfactory KYC and AML being carried out on proposed new noteholders that have pledged a total of £500k.
All other details of the New Loan Facility remain unchanged and are as set out in the Company's announcement of 6 July 2026.

company_30s.what_they_do: AIQ Ltd operates in the AI‑powered analytics space, providing cloud‑based tools that help businesses turn raw data into actionable insights. Its flagship product is an automated decision‑support platform that integrates with existing ERP systems.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The firm taps into the growing demand for AI‑driven efficiency across industries—from finance to manufacturing. Its technology offers a lower‑cost alternative to traditional analytics suites, giving it a competitive edge in a market that is rapidly expanding into the billions.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a restructuring phase, having issued convertible loan notes to shore up its balance sheet. It is trading at the very bottom of its 52‑week range, indicating a severe sell‑off that has wiped out a large portion of its market value.

rns_narrative: The latest filings show AIQ is actively managing its debt load: it issued convertible loan notes in August, updated the terms in mid‑August, and announced a new loan agreement in March. The company’s directors have also changed, hinting at a shift in strategy.
Results from the interim and annual reports suggest the business is still operating at a loss, but it has begun to reduce its burn rate by tightening costs and cutting non‑essential spend.
Collectively, these moves point to a company that is trying to stabilize its finances while keeping the door open for future growth.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism from a single voice
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are banking on the debt conversion and the possibility that the company will turn its loss profile into a cash‑positive operation once the notes mature.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the heavy debt load and lack of revenue could push the firm into further distress, especially if the convertible notes do not convert favourably.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has stayed flat; no new voices have joined the conversation, which keeps the market largely unaware of the company’s internal shifts.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends shows zero activity for AIQ, meaning any news or catalyst could spark a surprise move.

near_term_catalysts: The conversion of the 19‑August convertible notes could inject fresh equity and reduce debt, providing a clear financial catalyst.
A positive earnings report in the next quarterly filing may demonstrate that cost cuts are paying off, giving traders a tangible sign of improvement.
If the company announces a new partnership or product launch, it could signal a strategic pivot that attracts fresh investor interest.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to confirm a bounce include: (1) a sustained uptick in daily volume that outpaces the 20‑day moving average; (2) the price breaking the 200‑day moving average from below; and (3) a clear reversal in the short‑term RSI from oversold territory.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early phase of a crash‑recovery cycle. Capitulation is likely complete, but the market has yet to react to the potential debt conversion. The APEX score suggests the price is still in a compressed zone, ready for a spring.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: AIQ is trading at roughly 20% of its all‑time high. A bounce to 50% of that peak would represent a 150% gain. Deep crashes in the 70–95% range historically produce large rebounds, and the recent debt restructuring could provide the necessary catalyst.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still operates at a loss, and its debt load is sizeable. If the convertible notes do not convert or the market remains indifferent, the price could slide further toward its all‑time low.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 150% (from 20% to 50% of peak). Potential downside: limited to current price level; the worst case is a further drop to the 52‑week low, which would be a 80% decline from the peak. The asymmetry is therefore roughly 1:5.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback that closes above the 20‑day moving average, sizing the position so that a 5‑pence stop (roughly 10% of the entry price) keeps risk capped. Target the 50% of peak level, taking partial profits at 30% of peak to lock in gains.
playbook.if_watching: Hold off until you see a volume spike of at least 1.5× the 20‑day average and a break above the 200‑day moving average. Those are the clear confirmation signals.
playbook.if_passing: None identified; the company is not facing imminent delisting or bankruptcy.

ai_insights.bottom_line: AIQ sits at the bottom of a deep crash, and a timely debt conversion could trigger a mean‑reversion swing that delivers a 150% upside—making it a compelling contrarian play if the market remains oblivious.
